name: World Businesses for Sale
summary: International marketplace for buying and selling established businesses (restaurants, shops, services and manufacturers), free for buyers, with broker plans (listing fee plus 1-3% commission) or no-commission pay-as-you-go listings, and 24/7 guidance for sellers.
best_for: owners selling established, often brick-and-mortar businesses (restaurants, shops, services, small manufacturers) who want international buyer exposure with hands-on guidance
skip_if: you're selling a small online asset (an auction-style online-business marketplace fits better), or you want a free listing, even the cheapest no-commission plan here costs £49 a month
honest_knock: On the broker plans you pay twice: a listing fee up front AND commission when it sells (3% on Basic, 2% on Standard, 1% on Premium) on contracts of 6, 9 and 12 months. Only Premium stays live until sold with free renewals, so on the lower tiers a business that has not sold needs a paid renewal, and for a slow sale £999 once costs about the same as £499 twice. Every tier says commission is payable only when they introduce the buyer, which is exactly the clause to read in the contract before you sign. If you want no commission at all, the pay-as-you-go plans start at £49 a month, or £147 for six months: far cheaper up front, but those are listings, not broker introductions. As with any marketplace, the fee buys exposure, not a guaranteed sale.

pricing.entry_price_terms: a month (£147 per six months), broker plans from £395
pricing.notes: (2026, re-verified 2026-11-15 on their own store and selling pages) Browsing is free for buyers. Sellers pick one of two tracks. Broker plans: Basic £395 (3% commission, 6-month contract), Standard £499 (2% commission, 9 months), Premium £999 (1% commission, 12-month contract, stays live until sold with free renewals) — every tier states commission is due only if they introduce the buyer. Or no-commission pay-as-you-go listings (inc. VAT), now sold only as subscriptions: a Monthly Plan at Basic £49, Standard £75 or Premium £99 a month, or a 6-Month Plan at 50% off — £147, £225 or £297 per six months (the store's 'from £24.50/month'), renewing automatically every six months; you can cancel future renewals, and the listing stays active to the end of the paid period. You keep 100% of the sale price. Historical: until 15 October 2026 the broker plans were Standard £749 and Premium £1,500, and on 15 November 2026 the selling page showed £499 and £999. On 13 October 2026 we read these as one-off 30-day listings with 10% off monthly (£44.10 / £67.50 / £89.10) and 20% off for six months (£235.20 / £360.00 / £475.20). Free 24/7 chat guidance before you commit. Sources: broker plan prices, commissions and contract lengths from the selling page on 15 November 2026; pay-as-you-go prices from the no-commission page on 15 November 2026.

price_history.method: Stable = every amount on the vendor's pricing page identical across >= 3 of our reads over >= 30 days. A change is listed only after we confirmed the new price on the page, with a verbatim quote. Differences in raw readings are never published on their own.

compare_with.name: Flippa
compare_with.why: Flippa is the online-business marketplace (sites, apps, e-commerce) with auction dynamics; World Businesses for Sale leans brick-and-mortar and international with flat listing plans: pick by what you're actually selling

Commission never changes what a record says, and products are not ranked by commission. Where it is false the link is the vendor's plain site. exit_test.what: No account was needed; the tool ran without signing in. On 18 November 2026 the session browsed World Businesses for Sale without an account. The site has no filter panel, only a search box and a sort box. A search for e-commerce gave 31 results (11 of them plan or broker products) and a search for cafe gave 9 results, from GBP 78,500 to GBP 1,500,000. Annual turnover and net profit were shown openly and contact ran only through a form, which was not filled in. The broker plans are GBP 395, GBP 499 and GBP 999 with 3%, 2% and 1% commission, and the no-commission plans are GBP 49, GBP 75 and GBP 99 a month; all are the same as in the dossier, although the home page says from GBP 39 a month and quotes both 1% and 2% commission on different pages. Nothing was bought and nothing was put in the cart. Account and start: no account was used. Our AI assistant ran the test in a tab of our Chrome on worldbusinessesforsale.com, with no login (the interface is in English). The site opened on Netherlands | EUR with a cookie banner; cookies were declined (Decline) and the country and language were set to English with ?country=GB&language=en (United Kingdom | GBP). The dossier name is World Businesses for Sale and the review is on OSM (osm/world-businesses-for-sale-review.html). The test date is 18 Nov 2026; the start time was not recorded in the notes. Browse: there is NO filter panel (no country, sector or price filter): /collections/all shows 30 listings on 2 pages, with only a search box and a sort box (Relevance, Price, low to high, Price, high to low). Search 1: e-commerce gave 31 results (11 of them plan or broker products, not listings). The first listing was Successful E-Commerce Store, Niche Home Decor USA, GBP 350,000, Annual Turnover: $720,000, Net Profit: $160,000, location Austin, Texas. Turnover and profit are shown openly, without a login. Contact runs through the form Contact Us for More Information, which was not filled in. Search 2: cafe with the price sorted low to high gave 9 results, from GBP 78,500 (Ajman, UAE) to GBP 1,500,000 (New York), with Canada, Texas, London, Sao Paulo and Berlin in between; 1 was Sold. Four more e-commerce listings: Online Supermarket UK GBP 149,000; Pet Supplies Australia GBP 220,000; Tech Gadgets Australia GBP 1,800,000 (Sold); Online Supermarket Europe GBP 450,000. Sellers are anonymous and contact is only through the form; no login was needed. Plans: worldbusinessesforsale.com, read by the tester on 18 Nov 2026 with the country set to United Kingdom (GBP; the site first opened on Netherlands, EUR). Broker plans (/pages/sell-business): Basic GBP 395 (3%, 6 months), Standard GBP 499 (2%, 9 months, MOST POPULAR) and Premium GBP 999 (1%, 12 months, Stay Live Until Sold, Free Renewals); each says Pay commission only if we introduce the buyer. No-commission plans (/pages/sell-no-commission): Basic PAYG GBP 49, Standard GBP 75 and Premium GBP 99; 6-Month Plans from GBP 24.50/month inc. VAT, with GBP 147 payable upfront for six months; the page FAQ has the question Does My 6-Month Advertising Plan Renew Automatically? (the answer was not read). The home page says Sell Business No Commission from GBP 39 Per Month (Incl. VAT), the collection page says Sell your business with 2% commission! and the home page says Sell Your Business with 1% commission. With the country on the Netherlands the home page showed PAYG Basic EUR 59,95 and the 6-Month plan EUR 179,88. Advisory plans and a Founding Broker plan (from GBP 99) also exist; they were not opened. All broker and no-commission prices are the same as in the dossier, so the price is UNCHANGED; the line from GBP 39 a month is not in the dossier and is lower than the GBP 49 and GBP 24.50 on the plan page. Nothing was bought and nothing was put in the cart. A pop-up Get 20% Off (an e-mail field) was closed without filling it in and no screenshot of it was kept. Cancelling: not tested, nothing was bought. Not tested: the contact form, placing a listing, paying, cancelling and Klarna; the sellers of online businesses (the Flippa group) were not tested. Clean up: nothing was created; the own tab was closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: There is no filter panel, so a buyer can only search and sort. A search for e-commerce counts 11 plan or broker products among its 31 results. Three pages quote three different commission or monthly figures: from GBP 39 a month on the home page against GBP 49 on the plan page, and 1% on the home page against 2% on the collection page. Sellers are anonymous and contact runs only through a form.

exit_test.what: No account was needed; the tool ran without signing in. On 18 November 2026 the session browsed World Businesses for Sale without an account. The site has no filter panel, only a search box and a sort box. A search for e-commerce gave 31 results (11 of them plan or broker products) and a search for cafe gave 9 results, from GBP 78,500 to GBP 1,500,000. Annual turnover and net profit were shown openly and contact ran only through a form, which was not filled in. The broker plans are GBP 395, GBP 499 and GBP 999 with 3%, 2% and 1% commission, and the no-commission plans are GBP 49, GBP 75 and GBP 99 a month; all are the same as in the dossier, although the home page says from GBP 39 a month and quotes both 1% and 2% commission on different pages. Nothing was bought and nothing was put in the cart. Account and start: no account was used. Our AI assistant ran the test in a tab of our Chrome on worldbusinessesforsale.com, with no login (the interface is in English). The site opened on Netherlands | EUR with a cookie banner; cookies were declined (Decline) and the country and language were set to English with ?country=GB&language=en (United Kingdom | GBP). The dossier name is World Businesses for Sale and the review is on OSM (osm/world-businesses-for-sale-review.html). The test date is 18 Nov 2026; the start time was not recorded in the notes. Browse: there is NO filter panel (no country, sector or price filter): /collections/all shows 30 listings on 2 pages, with only a search box and a sort box (Relevance, Price, low to high, Price, high to low). Search 1: e-commerce gave 31 results (11 of them plan or broker products, not listings). The first listing was Successful E-Commerce Store, Niche Home Decor USA, GBP 350,000, Annual Turnover: $720,000, Net Profit: $160,000, location Austin, Texas. Turnover and profit are shown openly, without a login. Contact runs through the form Contact Us for More Information, which was not filled in. Search 2: cafe with the price sorted low to high gave 9 results, from GBP 78,500 (Ajman, UAE) to GBP 1,500,000 (New York), with Canada, Texas, London, Sao Paulo and Berlin in between; 1 was Sold. Four more e-commerce listings: Online Supermarket UK GBP 149,000; Pet Supplies Australia GBP 220,000; Tech Gadgets Australia GBP 1,800,000 (Sold); Online Supermarket Europe GBP 450,000. Sellers are anonymous and contact is only through the form; no login was needed. Plans: worldbusinessesforsale.com, read by the tester on 18 Nov 2026 with the country set to United Kingdom (GBP; the site first opened on Netherlands, EUR). Broker plans (/pages/sell-business): Basic GBP 395 (3%, 6 months), Standard GBP 499 (2%, 9 months, MOST POPULAR) and Premium GBP 999 (1%, 12 months, Stay Live Until Sold, Free Renewals); each says Pay commission only if we introduce the buyer. No-commission plans (/pages/sell-no-commission): Basic PAYG GBP 49, Standard GBP 75 and Premium GBP 99; 6-Month Plans from GBP 24.50/month inc. VAT, with GBP 147 payable upfront for six months; the page FAQ has the question Does My 6-Month Advertising Plan Renew Automatically? (the answer was not read). The home page says Sell Business No Commission from GBP 39 Per Month (Incl. VAT), the collection page says Sell your business with 2% commission! and the home page says Sell Your Business with 1% commission. With the country on the Netherlands the home page showed PAYG Basic EUR 59,95 and the 6-Month plan EUR 179,88. Advisory plans and a Founding Broker plan (from GBP 99) also exist; they were not opened. All broker and no-commission prices are the same as in the dossier, so the price is UNCHANGED; the line from GBP 39 a month is not in the dossier and is lower than the GBP 49 and GBP 24.50 on the plan page. Nothing was bought and nothing was put in the cart. A pop-up Get 20% Off (an e-mail field) was closed without filling it in and no screenshot of it was kept. Cancelling: not tested, nothing was bought. Not tested: the contact form, placing a listing, paying, cancelling and Klarna; the sellers of online businesses (the Flippa group) were not tested. Clean up: nothing was created; the own tab was closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: There is no filter panel, so a buyer can only search and sort. A search for e-commerce counts 11 plan or broker products among its 31 results. Three pages quote three different commission or monthly figures: from GBP 39 a month on the home page against GBP 49 on the plan page, and 1% on the home page against 2% on the collection page. Sellers are anonymous and contact runs only through a form.
